### A classical assessment {#projects-exam}

Since no mode is published, this design follows the balanced default of these notes: a written exam on the eight sessions, two graded labs and one project.

| Component | Weight | Format | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Written exam | 40 % | 2 h, no documents, one handwritten A4 sheet | ch. 0–10 |
| Lab reports | 25 % | Ex. 1 with part (e), the distortion of the mask measured against rejection (12.5 %), and Ex. 2 (12.5 %); notebook and 2-page note each | sessions 2–3 and 5 |
| Project | 35 % | one card of the [list below](#projects-list), or Ex. 6 extended into an attack report; report and 10-minute oral | sessions 1–8 |

**Resit.** A 2 h written exam on ch. 0–10 replaces the exam component; the lab and project marks are kept, and a missing project can be handed in once more and graded on the same grid.

**Sample questions.** Five questions of 4 points each, a 20-point paper of 2 h.

**Q1 (4 pts) — Masked decoding is not conditioning.** Vocabulary $\{a, b\}$, outputs of two tokens, constraint $S = \{aa, ba, bb\}$, and the model
$$
p(a) = p(b) = \tfrac12, \qquad p(a \mid a) = 0.2, \quad p(b \mid a) = 0.8, \qquad p(a \mid b) = p(b \mid b) = \tfrac12 .
$$
(a) Give the law of masked decoding on $S$. (b) Give the exact conditional law. (c) How many draws does rejection sampling need on average, and which weight turns masked samples into exact ones?

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

- (a) Step 1 masks nothing, since both letters can still reach $S$. After *a* only *a* survives ($Z_2 = 0.2$) and is renormalized to 1. Masked law: *aa* 0.5, *ba* 0.25, *bb* 0.25 (1.5 pts).
- (b) The constraint has probability 0.1 + 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.6, so the exact law is *aa* 1/6 ≈ 0.167, *ba* and *bb* 5/12 ≈ 0.417 each (1 pt).
- (c) The number of draws is geometric with success probability 0.6, hence 1/0.6 ≈ 1.67 draws on average (0.5 pt). The weight is the product of the normalizers: 0.2 for *aa*, 1 for *ba* and *bb*. Self-normalized, 0.5 × 0.2 : 0.25 : 0.25 gives back 1/6, 5/12, 5/12 (1 pt). Common error: calling the mask exact because every output lies in $S$ (theorem 2.2).
:::

**Q2 (4 pts) — The closed form of RLHF.** (a) Show that the maximizer of the first objective below is the law on the right:
$$
\max_\pi\ \mathbb{E}_{y \sim \pi}\big[r(x, y)\big] - \beta\, \mathrm{KL}\big(\pi \,\|\, \pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\big), \qquad \pi^*(y \mid x) = \frac{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y \mid x)\, e^{r(x, y)/\beta}}{Z(x)} .
$$
(b) Three answers have reference probabilities 0.5, 0.3, 0.2 and rewards 0, 1, 2; with $\beta = 1$, compute $\pi^*$. (c) Describe the limits $\beta \to \infty$ and $\beta \to 0$, and name the quantity of classifier-free guidance that plays the role of $1/\beta$.

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

- (a) Rewrite the objective as
  $$
  -\beta\, \mathrm{KL}(\pi \,\|\, \pi^*) + \beta \log Z(x) ;
  $$
  the KL is nonnegative and vanishes only at $\pi = \pi^*$, which gives the maximizer and its uniqueness (2 pts). The first-order derivation of theorem 5.1 is accepted.
- (b) Weights $(0.5,\ 0.3e,\ 0.2e^2) = (0.5,\ 0.815,\ 1.478)$, normalizer 2.793, so $\pi^* \approx (0.179,\ 0.292,\ 0.529)$ (1 pt).
- (c) A large $\beta$ gives back the reference law; a small $\beta$ puts all the mass on the answer of largest reward (the third). The guidance strength $w$ of theorem 7.1 plays the role of $1/\beta$ (1 pt). Common error: forgetting the normalizer $Z(x)$, or multiplying the reward by $\beta$.
:::

**Q3 (4 pts) — Watermark test and its power.** The green fraction is $\gamma = 0.25$, and a suspect text has 100 tokens, 40 of them green.

(a) Compute $z$ and decide at level $10^{-3}$, whose quantile is 3.09. (b) A marked text draws a green token with probability $p_\delta = 0.4$: compute the expected $z$ for 100 tokens, then the length needed for a power of 0.9 at the threshold $z = 4$ (the 0.9 quantile is 1.28). (c) What happens to this length if $p_\delta - \gamma$ is halved?

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

- (a) The score is above the threshold, so H0 is rejected and the text is flagged, with a $p$-value of about $2.7 \times 10^{-4}$ (1 pt):
  $$
  z = \frac{40 - 25}{\sqrt{100 \times 0.25 \times 0.75}} = \frac{15}{4.33} \approx 3.46 > 3.09 .
  $$
- (b) Expected score $0.15 \times 10 / 0.433 \approx 3.46$ (0.5 pt). With the length formula of theorem 6.2 (1.5 pts),
  $$
  T \approx \left(\frac{4 \times 0.433 + 1.28 \times 0.490}{0.15}\right)^2 \approx 15.7^2 \approx 247 \text{ tokens}.
  $$
- (c) The length scales as $(p_\delta - \gamma)^{-2}$: it is multiplied by 4 (1 pt). Common errors: the H1 standard deviation used under H0, or a two-sided quantile for this one-sided test.
:::

**Q4 (4 pts) — Hard constraint or guidance.** A law $p = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2)$ on three outputs has the admissible set $S = \{2, 3\}$.

(a) Give the law renormalized on $S$ and its entropy, and compare it with the ceiling of theorem 9.2. (b) For the exponential guidance $p_w \propto p\, e^{w c}$ with score $c = (0, 1, 1)$ and $w = 1$, compute the law, the fidelity $p_w(S)$ and the entropy. (c) Is the entropy monotone in $w$? Justify.

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

- (a) The law (0, 0.6, 0.4) has entropy 0.673 nats, below the ceiling $\log 2 \approx 0.693$ (1 pt).
- (b) Weights (0.5, 0.815, 0.544) with sum 1.859, law (0.269, 0.439, 0.292), fidelity 0.731 (against 0.5 without guidance), entropy 1.074 nats (1.5 pts).
- (c) No: the entropy of $p$ is 1.030 nats, so guidance first *raises* it. With the derivative of Ex. 4,
  $$
  \frac{dH}{dw} = -\mathrm{Cov}_w(\log p, c) - w\, \mathrm{Var}_w(c), \qquad \mathrm{Cov}_p(\log p, c) \approx -0.168 ,
  $$
  the slope at $w = 0$ is positive: mass moves from the most likely output to rarer admissible ones. As $w \to \infty$, the law tends to that of (a) (1.5 pts). Common error: "guidance always lowers diversity".
:::

**Q5 (4 pts) — Diagnosis.** A team plugs a JSON-schema mask into its agent and reports: "100 % valid tool calls, so control is solved, and it is free." (a) Give two measurements that test "free". (b) Give one failure that the mask cannot prevent, and the defense of ch. 10.

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

- (a) Any two of (1 pt each): the fidelity/diversity curve with and without the mask, since reporting fidelity alone is the anti-protocol of proposition 9.3; the distortion of theorem 2.2, by comparing masked outputs with rejection sampling on a sample of prompts, or by the spread of the weights $\prod_t Z_t$; the time overhead per token and the one-off cost of compiling the index.
- (b) The mask guarantees syntax, never semantics: a valid call can carry an injected instruction or a wrong value (a date 31/02), and an ambiguous grammar can blow up the automaton (1 pt). Defense: downstream semantic validation with bounds, limits on the number of states, server-side precompiled grammars (1 pt).
:::

### Projects {#projects-list}

Every project uses public data, a laptop CPU or one free Colab T4 GPU, and only what this module, its prerequisites (Large Language Models, Graph ML, one Deep Learning course) and the mandatory LLM course of the same period teach. Levels ★/★★/★★★ are those of the exercises, and the effort stays at most 20 h per student, as for a 24 h / 2 ECTS course.

**Grading grid used by every project of this page** (a project card may replace one row).

| Criterion | Weight |
|---|---|
| Question and success metric stated before the experiments | 10 % |
| Correct use of the course results (cited by number) | 25 % |
| Protocol: leakage-free split, baselines, at least 3 seeds, intervals | 25 % |
| Results and analysis: error analysis, limits, one responsible-AI remark | 20 % |
| Reproducibility: repository, README, pinned environment, one command | 10 % |
| Communication: report (≤ 6 pages solo, ≤ 10 group) or 10-minute oral | 10 % |

Group projects: a contribution statement and an oral with individual questions; the individual grade is the group grade times a factor in [0.8, 1.2].

#### P1 · ★★ · solo · Watermark under paraphrase {#proj-1}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | Measure how paraphrasing erodes the green/red watermark (Definition 6.1): report the AUC of the z-test and the median $z$ at 200 tokens, before and after paraphrase, against the unigram scheme of proposition 6.4 as baseline. |
| Data | [C4 realnewslike](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/c4) — ODC-By 1.0 — ≈ 13.8 M news-like web documents, of which 500 serve as prompts and 500 as human texts; loading: `load_dataset("allenai/c4", "realnewslike", split="validation", streaming=True)`; generator and paraphraser [Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) (Apache 2.0) |
| Chapters | [ch. 6](#ch6) (Definition 6.1, theorem 6.2, proposition 6.4), [ch. 9](#ch9), [ch. 10](#ch10) (proposition 10.2); extends Ex. 2 and Ex. 6 ([exercises](#ex)) |
| Deliverables | notebook and 4-page report |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 18 h per student · free Colab T4 (1.5B model in fp16), longest run ≤ 90 min (1,000 generations of 200 tokens and 500 paraphrases) |
| Objectives served | O8 (provenance, robustness), O3 (LLM decoding) |
| Specific criterion | Replaces the protocol row: same prompts, keys and $(\gamma, \delta)$ for both schemes, false-positive rate measured on the 500 human texts, threshold fixed before the attack (25 %). |
| Responsible AI | C4 texts are written by people: publish only aggregate statistics, never the texts; discuss the false accusation of human authors (spoofing, proposition 10.2). |
| Going further | Spoofing: estimate the green lists from marked outputs and forge the mark on human texts. |

#### P2 · ★★ · solo · Steering vectors versus DPO {#proj-2}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | On the IMDB controlled-sentiment task, compare ActAdd steering (Definition 4.1) with a LoRA-DPO fine-tune (proposition 5.2): report the positive-sentiment rate, the perplexity under the base model and the distinct-2 diversity of 500 continuations, against unsteered GPT-2, and draw both fidelity/diversity curves (proposition 9.3). |
| Data | [IMDB](https://huggingface.co/datasets/stanfordnlp/imdb) — research use (Maas et al., 2011) — 50,000 movie reviews, whose first 8 tokens serve as prompts; loading: `load_dataset("stanfordnlp/imdb", split="test")`; model [GPT-2 small](https://huggingface.co/openai-community/gpt2) (MIT); sentiment judge [DistilBERT SST-2](https://huggingface.co/distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english) (Apache 2.0), which also labels the DPO preference pairs |
| Chapters | [ch. 4](#ch4) (Definition 4.1, proposition 4.3), [ch. 5](#ch5) (theorem 5.1, proposition 5.2), [ch. 9](#ch9); LoRA and DPO training: [Large Language Models](../m2-large-language-models/index.html#ch4) ch. 4–5 (same period, sessions 4–5); extends Ex. 3 |
| Deliverables | notebook and 4-page report |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 18 h per student · free Colab T4, longest run ≤ 60 min (LoRA-DPO on 5,000 pairs) |
| Objectives served | O3 (post-training as control), O1 (first-order analysis of steering) |
| Responsible AI | Reviews are used as prompts only; report the error rate of the judge on 100 hand-labelled continuations, since optimizing a flawed judge is the reward hacking of ch. 5. |
| Going further | Two steering directions at once (sentiment and formality) and their interference. |

#### P3 · ★★ · group (3–4) · Grammar-constrained molecule generation and its distortion {#proj-3}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | Train a small SMILES language model and compare unconstrained sampling, a syntax and valence mask (ch. 3, theorem 8.1) and rejection sampling: report validity, uniqueness, novelty and FCD on 10,000 samples, and the distortion of the mask with respect to the exact rejection law (total variation on ring and atom-type statistics, spread of the weights of theorem 2.2). |
| Data | [ZINC250k via TDC](https://tdcommons.ai/generation_tasks/molgen/) — ZINC terms: free to use for everyone — 249,455 molecules as SMILES; loading: `from tdc.generation import MolGen; MolGen(name="ZINC").get_data()`; RDKit (BSD) for validity, `fcd_torch` for FCD |
| Chapters | [ch. 2](#ch2) (theorem 2.2, proposition 2.3), [ch. 3](#ch3) (proposition 3.2, theorem 3.3), [ch. 8](#ch8), [ch. 9](#ch9); molecule metrics: [Graph ML](../m1p2-graph-ml/index.html#ch9) 9.6 |
| Deliverables | repository with a one-command run, 8-page report, 10-minute oral with individual questions |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 12 h per student · free Colab T4, longest run ≤ 60 min (3-layer LSTM or 10M-parameter transformer on 250k SMILES) |
| Objectives served | O2 (graph generation), O4 (molecular graphs), O6 (chemistry) |
| Specific criterion | Replaces the course-results row: the distortion is measured against the exact rejection law and explained with the normalizers of theorem 2.2 (25 %). |
| Responsible AI | Dual use: report distributional metrics only, give no synthesis route, and do not optimize toxicity-related properties. |
| Going further | Sequential Monte Carlo with the weights of theorem 2.2, then the graph-native decoders of Graph Generative Models (period 2). |

#### P4 · ★★★ · group (3–4) · Knowledge-graph extraction with JSON-schema decoding {#proj-4}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | Extract (subject, relation, object) triples from WebNLG texts with a 1.5B instruction model under free decoding, JSON-schema decoding (ch. 3) and schema decoding plus semantic validation (ch. 10): report the valid-JSON rate, triple precision, recall and F1 against the gold triples, and the accuracy of 100 templated questions answered over the extracted graph, against free decoding. |
| Data | [WebNLG 2020, release 3.0 (English)](https://gitlab.com/shimorina/webnlg-dataset) — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — ≈ 16,600 sets of 1 to 7 DBpedia triples with reference texts (test: 1,779); loading: `git clone --depth 1 https://gitlab.com/shimorina/webnlg-dataset`, then parse `release_v3.0/en/*/*.xml` with `xml.etree`; model [Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) with the [Outlines](https://github.com/dottxt-ai/outlines) library (Apache 2.0) |
| Chapters | [ch. 3](#ch3) (theorem 3.3, the JSON Schema note), [ch. 9](#ch9), [ch. 10](#ch10) (theorem 10.1); knowledge graphs: [Graph ML](../m1p2-graph-ml/index.html#ch10) ch. 10 |
| Deliverables | repository with a one-command run, 8-page report, 10-minute oral with individual questions |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 15 h per student · free Colab T4, longest run ≤ 2 h (1,779 test texts under three decodings) |
| Objectives served | O5 (LLMs with graphs), O3 (structured generation), O4 (knowledge graphs) |
| Specific criterion | Replaces the course-results row: an error taxonomy that separates syntax errors (removed by the mask) from semantic ones (wrong relation, invented entity), on 50 hand-checked cases (25 %). |
| Responsible AI | Many triples describe real people: an invented triple is a false statement about a person, so report its rate and do not publish the extracted graph (non-commercial share-alike licence). |
| Going further | The larger relation inventory of [REBEL](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Babelscape/rebel-dataset) (CC BY-SA 4.0), or exact conditioning on the schema by sequential Monte Carlo. |

### End-of-year projects {#projects-capstone}

Five Year-2 capstones of the transverse project use this module: schema-constrained answers, tool calls or analyst notes (ch. 3) in [C1](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c1), [C2](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c2), [C5](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c5) and [C7](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c7), with watermarked outputs (ch. 6) in C7; molecular masks and guidance in [C3](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c3), whose research variant measures the distortion of theorem 2.2. The module brings to all of them one habit: measure every control by its fidelity/diversity curve, with and without an attacker (ch. 9–10).
